title: This Pig's Tusks Grow Through Its Face and Can Pierce Its Own Skull

scenes.text: This pig's teeth are growing straight into its own skull.
The babirusa lives on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi. Up to 220 pounds, and it can run 30 miles an hour.
In the males, the upper canines grow up through the top of the snout, break out through the skin, and curve back toward the forehead.
They never stop growing. Over a foot long, curling back toward the skull they came out of.
Grow long enough, and a tusk can pierce the skull. It's rare, because the tusks are brittle and usually snap first.
They're useless in a fight. Males box with their front legs instead. So why grow a tooth that can kill you? Nobody knows.

description:
The babirusa, a wild pig from Sulawesi and nearby Indonesian islands, grows upper canine tusks that erupt through the top of its snout and curve back toward its forehead.
The tusks keep growing for life, can exceed a foot in length, and in rare cases curl far enough to pierce the animal's own skull; they are too brittle to fight with, so males box with their front legs. Around 10,000 remain in the wild.
What other animal is built in a way that makes no sense?
subject: babirusa
first_comment: People on Sulawesi were drawing babirusas on cave walls 35,000 years ago, among the oldest animal paintings on Earth. Which animal has the strangest teeth you know?
